attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own post. He is not quoting anyone. The 'darker predictions' that follow do not withdraw this claim.

semantics.note: 'Will surely' and 'I guarantee' are firm language, so this is a scored forecast. The release condition and the comparison to GPT-4 are both kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (a substantial overall advance over GPT-4) is a fair, ordinary reading. In context, 'minds blown' and 'totally eclipse' are emphasis about how big the advance is. Excluding o3 and GPT-4o as comparators matches his words.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own dated announcement. It is used only to show the release condition was met (7 Aug 2025). As a company disclosure, it cannot show GPT-5 was better.

Independent Epoch analysis, dated Aug 2025. It finds GPT-5 far ahead of GPT-4 on several notable benchmarks, a large advance. It notes caveats: GPT-4 snapshots were substituted, benchmark choice was subjective, and reception was mixed.
OpenAI restored GPT-4o on 12 Aug 2025. GPT-4o is a different comparator, so this says nothing about how GPT-5 compares with GPT-4.

reviews.rationale: GPT-5 was released on 7 Aug 2025. Epoch's dated, independent analysis shows large benchmark gains over GPT-4 across several domains. That meets the support condition and the early-resolution rule. Epoch also notes a mixed reception, but 'minds blown' is read as rhetoric about the size of the advance, so this does not change the result. The GPT-4o restoration concerns a different model.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own post, stated as one of his predictions.

semantics.note: 'Won't' is firm, so this is a forecast. It is a conjunction of three parts. The 'without external aids' condition and the Rosie comparison are both kept.

contract.note: Reading 'beat' as reproducible wins and 'reliable driving' as sustained safe driving is ordinary. The contract admits that 'external aids' and Rosie-like versatility are undefined. Each part can be contradicted on its own.

evidence.note: Butter-Bench (Oct 2025) tested GPT-5 on a narrow set of robot delivery tasks. GPT-5 scored well below humans, but the robot was run through an interface and the tasks are not Rosie-like versatility. It does not cover Diplomacy or driving.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no controlled test of GPT-5 against Cicero and no sustained driving evaluation. The only robot study is narrow and uses an interface. None of the three parts is shown or contradicted, and the claim has no deadline. Under the contract, absence of evidence settles nothing.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Won't' is firm, so this is a forecast. The scope ('natural language output') and the 'simply and directly' qualifier are both kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (dependable behaviour when free-form output drives a program) is fair. Excluding tool calls and code generation keeps to his scope. He gave no error threshold.

evidence.note: Microsoft demo (Aug 2025): GPT-5 sends SQL and Python to tools inside an execution loop. It is a single run with no reliability data, and the output is executable code rather than direct use of natural-language output.

reviews.rationale: No item in the packet tests representative direct integrations of GPT-5's natural-language output against stated reliability requirements. The Microsoft demo uses tool-calling with code in a loop and gives no reliability figures. The claim has no deadline and the evidence does not settle it.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'Won't' is firm, so this is a forecast. The 'by itself' qualifier is kept.

contract.note: Reading the claim as broad competence on unfamiliar tasks, rather than literally every task, is ordinary and fair. The contract admits there is no operational definition of AGI.

evidence.note: Spatial-intelligence study (Aug 2025): GPT-5 falls short of human level in several fundamental spatial capabilities. This is partial support, from one task family under fixed prompts and token budgets.
The same study finds state-of-the-art results and some human-level scores. This does not show general intelligence.

reviews.rationale: The support condition requires persistent failures to generalise across ordinary task families, after reasonable efforts to draw out the model's ability. The packet has one spatial study under fixed settings. It shows gaps in one domain but not broad limits, and the packet's own stated gaps admit this. Nothing shows broad competence either. The claim has no deadline and is unresolved on this packet.
